title: Hard tenant isolation: burst pools, enforced hard quotas, and noisy-neighbor detection
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a production-grade tenant isolation system for Dedicated that provides: (1) guaranteed baseline throughput per tenant, (2) controlled burst capacity via per-tenant burst pools, (3) hard and soft quota enforcement to prevent cross-tenant resource exhaustion, and (4) automated noisy-neighbor detection and mitigation with minimal customer-visible disruption.

Background: Customers on Dedicated have asked for stronger isolation guarantees beyond soft quotas and best-effort limits. Current soft-quota system (ENG-9821) reduces but does not eliminate noisy neighbor incidents. This ticket designs and implements a combined admission-control + scheduling + telemetry approach that aims for deterministic throughput and enforceable hard limits for committed capacity.

Scope / Non-goals:
- In scope: scheduler changes to pin GPU slots to tenant slices, a lightweight per-tenant burst pool backed by reserved GPU slab capacity, enforcement hooks in the admission and driver layers to block allocation beyond hard quota, instrumentation for noisy-neighbor signals (latency, kernel stalls, GPU SM saturation), and a canary rollout path for Dedicated customers.
- Out of scope: full hypervisor-level isolation or per-tenant virtualized GPUs (separate project if customers require HBM-level fencing). This ticket focuses on orchestration and runtime enforcement within our current runtime.

Design summary:
1) Physical partitioning concept: maintain logical 'slices' of the fleet where each slice maps to a subset of GPU slabs (by rack/host labels). Slices are configured per-customer or per-commitment tier. Baseline throughput is enforced by reserving a fraction of slab slots for the tenant (hard reservation).
2) Burst pools: provide a small shared pool of capacity they can use when idle. Burst pools are filled from an overprovision buffer and gated by a per-tenant token bucket. Burst consumption is transient and subject to preemption when a different tenant's hard reservation needs capacity.
3) Hard and soft quotas: soft quotas continue to provide notifications and throttling at the API edge. Hard quotas are enforced via the admission controller in the scheduler—requests that would exceed a tenant's hard quota are rejected with structured errors and a Retry-After header when applicable.
4) Noisy-neighbor detection: implement a detector that aggregates signals: per-GPU kernel queue depth, SM utilization, long tail latency on token generation, excessive KV cache evictions, and OOM/oom-killer-like failures. If a host / slab shows correlated signs tied to a tenant, mitigation steps escalate: (a) throttle the offending tenant's requests, (b) move non-critical jobs off the host, (c) in severe cases, reprovision dedicated slab slices and surface incident to SRE and customer.
5) Metrics and observability: expose new per-tenant metrics (allocated_slots, burst_tokens, hard_quota_used, noisy_neighbor_score) to the Console and to internal alerting. Provide per-host heatmaps to help SRE diagnose cross-tenant interference.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 1 (Spike, 1 week): prototype admission-controller hook and token-bucket burst pool in staging, correlate with existing telemetry (ENG-11890). Deliverable: small prototype PR and docs.
- Phase 2 (Scheduler + Runtime, 3 weeks): implement slab-slicing config, admission enforcement for hard quotas, and preemption policy. Deliverable: runtime-2.4 branch PRs, integration tests.
- Phase 3 (Detector + Mitigation, 2 weeks): noisy-neighbor scoring service, mitigation actions (throttle/migrate), and playbook for SRE.
- Phase 4 (Canary + Rollout, 2 weeks): enable for 2 low-risk Dedicated customers, monitor metrics, iterate on thresholds.

Acceptance criteria:
- No customer can exceed their hard quota in steady state (verified by integration tests and canary).
- Burst behavior conforms to token-bucket semantics and is preemptible within 2s of a higher-priority hard allocation event.
- Noisy-neighbor detector identifies >90% of injected interference in synthetic tests and triggers mitigation actions without false-positive rate >5%.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Tenant+Isolation+Design+v2 (working draft)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3218 (Phase 1)
- Scheduler PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/448 (branch: eng/ENG-12786-slab-slicing)
- Load tests: https://internal-grafana.redwood.ai/d/loads/tenant-isolation?orgId=1 (dashboard created)

Rollout plan & customer comms:
- Start with customers who opted into stronger isolation (Customer A, Customer B). Provide playbook and monitored rollout for 3 weeks.
- For Dedicated customers that prefer soft behavior, keep opt-out flag. Default for new Dedicated customers in runtime-2.4 will be 'hard-isolation-enabled' for commit-tier plans.

Risk & trade-offs:
- Hard reservations reduce overall statistical multiplexing and could increase cost for customers and for Redwood. Mitigation: tune slice granularity, and offer dynamic sizing APIs so customers can shrink/expand reservations.
- Migration and preemption may cause transiently higher latencies for batch workloads. We'll add latency SLO windows to the canary plan.
- Incorrect detector thresholds can either under-protect customers or over-throttle. We'll use conservative defaults, require SRE approval, and have a rapid rollback path.

Next steps (short-term):
- Finish scheduler PR and open implementation PR for the admission controller by 2026-03-12.
- Coordinate with SRE (James O'Leary) and Console team (Priya Nair) for metrics and alerts.
- Schedule security review with Compliance by 2026-03-18.
